## Repeat the nearest owned cell (`extrapolation`) {#sec-ch11-extrapolation}

### Summary

The extrapolation callback is the simplest open boundary: it imposes no state and no wave selection, only a
vanishing normal gradient at the face. It is the implicit choice for every quantity that the characteristic
boundary cannot or need not split, which is why the outflow callback routes auxiliary scalar fields and the
shallow-water system through it.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Repeat the nearest owned value; @eq-ch11-extrapolation-copy.

**Data.** One owned cell supplies all ghost depths; units unchanged.

**Placement.** Physical fill, also the scalar and shallow-water outflow fallback.

**Activation.** Set `extrapolation` on an external face; default off.

**Guarantee / limits.** Constant preserving; no characteristic selection.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test limits are in the Tests layer; solver ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

### Derivation

For a smooth field with a prescribed zero normal derivative, a constant extension supplies ghost values.
The discrete rule is the nearest owned-cell average repeated at every ghost depth:

$$
q_{i-l}=q_i.
$$ {#eq-ch11-extrapolation-copy}

At the lower wall $i$ is the first owned index and $l=1,\ldots,n_g$; the upper rule uses the last owned cell.
`extrapolation_inner`
([`bc_func.cpp:52-66`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L52-L66))
and its upper-wall twin `extrapolation_outer` implement @eq-ch11-extrapolation-copy by assigning a width-one
slab to the width-$n_g$ ghost slab, which broadcasts it. For a general smooth field, a Taylor expansion between
the donor and the ghost centroids gives a leading difference proportional to their separation times the normal
derivative, hence $O(h)$ at fixed depth on a uniform grid. This is a consistency estimate for ghost values, not
a measured solver convergence rate. Check C1 verifies exact constant preservation and idempotence [check
`src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch11/checks/boundary_check.out`]. The checks do not
call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

A collapsed direction returns at once. Primitive, conserved and scalar calls all use the same copy; no row is
treated specially. `radiating` ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}) selects this copy before any of its
own checks when the input type is `kScalar` or the EOS type is `shallow-water`, so an auxiliary limiter field
and a tracer density under outflow never go through the acoustic split. The callback runs with the physical
fills of @sec-ch11-timing, including the corner refresh after an exchange.

@fig-ch11-extrapolation-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

### Code

**How to use.** Use this fragment for an open face with a zero-gradient copy. It supplies no exterior pressure and
does not remove incoming acoustic modes.

This is a configuration fragment, not a standalone simulation deck.

```yaml
boundary-condition:
  external:
    x1-inner: extrapolation
    x1-outer: extrapolation
```

**Refusals and prerequisites.** The callback has no state-admissibility refusal and returns for a collapsed
direction. The parser rejects unknown names and keys as described in @sec-ch11-registry.

**Read the implementation.** `extrapolation_inner` ({{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp >}}) contains:

```cpp
var.narrow(dim, 0, nghost) = var.narrow(dim, nghost, 1);
```

Broadcasting the width-one donor realizes @eq-ch11-extrapolation-copy at every ghost depth.

| radiating | {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}} | `radiating` | `outflow` |

: Implementation sites for extrapolation. {#tbl-ch11-extrapolation-code}

1. Select the first or last owned width-one slab. The anchor `extrapolation_inner` is in
   [`bc_func.cpp:52-66`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L52-L66).
2. Broadcast it to the whole ghost slab without changing owned cells. The anchor `extrapolation_outer` is in
   [`bc_func.cpp:52-66`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L52-L66).
3. Use the same operation as the scalar and shallow-water fallback of outflow. The anchor `radiating` is in
   {{< code src/bc/bc_func.cpp radiating >}}.

**Not provided:** a round-off derivation for each tolerance, because the cited tests give acceptance

The report-only checks `[C1]` establish that copy, parity, idempotence and corner ownership hold
exactly.[^ch11-extrapolation-run]
These checks exercise report formulas, not the compiled boundary kernels. The source-test table records
assertions and tolerances, not new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver results.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A zero gradient is not an acoustic nonreflection condition. The pulse test prints the extrapolation arm but
asserts only the outflow arm, so no measured reflection fraction for extrapolation is claimed.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
